Above 1, one request translates several consecutive sentences, which is usually faster and cheaper, though translation quality may vary slightly. If the answer to a batch is incomplete, malformed, cut off for length or refused by the model, or the request runs past its time limit (times out), the batch is automatically split into smaller ones and retried; a stream that sends no data for too long (idle timeout) and network or provider errors are retried or reported just as with one sentence per request. If you also set an output limit, allow about 150–300 tokens per sentence, plus room for the thinking output when thinking is on.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: LectureFlow is a program that runs on your own computer. This page explains what it keeps, and what it sends where and when.
privacy.local.title: What stays on this computer
privacy.local.1: Your recordings and videos, lectures fetched through the browser extension, syllabi and slides are kept in LectureFlow's data folder.
privacy.local.2: Speech recognition, text extraction, playback and subtitles all happen on this computer. Recordings are not sent to any model service. They leave this computer only if you choose remote transcription: for Google Colab, see below; with a remote server you added yourself, the recording and the transcription prompt (English terms from the glossary) are uploaded over encrypted SSH to that server. LectureFlow deletes the files there at once when the result is back on this computer (or after a cancel or a transcription error on the server); in other cases (for example an unfinished upload or a dropped connection), they expire about 2 hours after the connection ends and are deleted the next time LectureFlow connects to the server after that; if it never connects again, they stay there.
privacy.local.3: Transcripts, translations, glossaries and your edits are kept in a database on this computer.
privacy.sent.title: What is sent to model services
privacy.sent.1: LectureFlow only contacts a model service (such as DeepSeek) after you have set it up.
privacy.sent.2: It sends the text needed for correction, translation and organizing: the transcribed sentences, the full text of the syllabus and the slides, the glossary, and the course name and course code. To title lectures and to work out the file-name rule it also sends the uploaded files' original names (for a lecture sent by the browser extension, the title on the web page or platform), their upload times and the creation times recorded in the media files, the term start date, and the names and codes of the lecture kinds (including those you added). The recording itself is never sent.
privacy.sent.3: You can see and change which service does what under “Roles” in Settings. The provider's own privacy policy applies to the text it receives.
privacy.sent.4: Some free services' terms allow the provider to use what you send to improve its models. If that matters to you, choose a paid service or the “Transcription only” plan.
privacy.keys.title: API keys
privacy.keys.1: API keys and the Colab authorization are stored encrypted in the database on this computer, protected by your system account (DPAPI on Windows, the Keychain on macOS). After moving the data folder to another computer or account, you enter them again. A key is only used for requests to its provider.
privacy.keys.2: The interface only shows the first and last few characters of a key; exported diagnostics never contain keys.
privacy.downloads.title: Component downloads and updates
privacy.downloads.1: On first use, LectureFlow downloads the runtime and models from the source you chose (default or a mirror) and verifies every file.
privacy.downloads.2: Updates are checked at most once a day, only at public release addresses (GitHub and mirrors you added); none of your data is sent. An update is installed only after its signature has been verified.
privacy.colab.title: Google Colab remote transcription
privacy.colab.1: Recordings are uploaded to Colab only if you turn on Google Colab remote transcription. They go to your own Colab session to be transcribed, and the results are downloaded back to this computer. Along with a recording goes the transcription prompt: English terms from the glossary, which help it recognize subject words. When several lectures are processed, the queued ones are uploaded ahead; by default they stay in the runtime's memory, and the remote files are deleted once the results are back.
privacy.colab.2: LectureFlow uses your Colab authorization to ask Google for your account's compute unit balance and the GPUs you can use, and reads the runtime's memory and GPU figures only while it is in use. This information is shown only on your computer.
privacy.none.title: What is not collected
privacy.none.1: LectureFlow collects no usage data, uploads no crash reports, and has no accounts or cloud sync.
privacy.none.2: “Export diagnostics” creates a file only when you select it, and you decide whether to share it. It never contains lecture content or API keys.
privacy.none.3: LectureFlow serves its interface only on this computer's loopback address; other devices on your network cannot reach it.
privacy.delete.title: Deleting
privacy.delete.1: Deleting a lecture also deletes its recording and results. However, the parts of model answers that could not be used (for example an answer in the wrong format) are kept in the logs on this computer (the logs/llm folder, for troubleshooting; only the beginning and end of a long answer) and are not deleted with the lecture; they expire after about 14 days and are deleted the next time LectureFlow sends a request to a model service. When log_level in config.toml is set to debug, whole requests and answers are kept there too; they are not deleted with the lecture either and expire by the same rule.
privacy.delete.2: After uninstalling LectureFlow, delete its data folder to remove everything.
privacy.footer: LectureFlow is open-source software (AGPL-3.0-or-later); everything described here can be checked in its source code.
privacy.ext.title: Browser extension
privacy.ext.1: The browser extension talks only to LectureFlow on this computer. It connects to no server and does not read course names, folders or materials.
privacy.ext.2: The extension reads the recording site's cookies only when you send a lecture. LectureFlow keeps them in memory for that fetch only and sends each cookie back only to the site it belongs to.
privacy.ext.3: The record of fetched lectures stays on this computer and keeps no page or media paths; the logs do not record them either.
